findings.issue: The MSA delegates all service credit amounts entirely to each Statement of Work, with no floor or cap set in the agreement itself. If a SOW is silent or poorly drafted, the Customer has no contractual backstop for service credits, leaving the remedy undefined and potentially unenforceable. This is a medium-severity gap that does not require senior-counsel escalation but should be tracked and remedied in each SOW.
findings.quote: If the Provider fails to meet a Service Level, the Provider shall credit the Customer with the service credits specified in the Statement of Work.
findings.quote_template: If the Provider fails to meet a Service Level, the Provider shall credit the Customer with the service credits specified in the Statement of Work.
findings.suggested_fix: If the Provider fails to meet a Service Level, the Provider shall credit the Customer with the service credits specified in the Statement of Work, which shall in no event be less than five percent (5%) nor more than ten percent (10%) of the monthly Fees attributable to the affected Service for each month in which the failure occurs.

findings.issue: The deliverables table (D1–D3), services description, acceptance criteria, and out-of-scope list all contain unfilled placeholder text (e.g., '[Deliverable name and description]', '[YYYY-MM-DD]', '[name]'). No actual deliverable is named, no due date is set, and no owner is identified, meaning the contract currently has no enforceable scope — the most common cause of disputes and overruns. This requires immediate completion before execution; no senior-counsel escalation is specified for this rule, but the contract should not be signed in this state.
